body:
### Summary

When installing from a `pylock.toml` that declares top-level `default-groups`, uv does not seed `dependency_groups` for marker evaluation, so packages gated on those groups are silently skipped. `pip` honors `default-groups` and installs the same file correctly.

PEP 751's [Installation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/#installation) steps say:

> Gather the extras and dependency groups to install and set `extras` and `dependency_groups` for marker evaluation, respectively.
> - `extras` SHOULD be set to the empty set by default.
> - **`dependency_groups` SHOULD be the set created from `default-groups` by default.**

#### Minimal reproducible example

`pylock.toml` (hand-written, one dependency-free wheel):

```toml
lock-version = "1.0"
default-groups = ["mygroup"]
created-by = "hand-written"

[[packages]]
name = "mypy-extensions"
version = "1.1.0"
marker = "\"mygroup\" in dependency_groups"
requires-python = ">=3.8"

[[packages.wheels]]
name = "mypy_extensions-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
url = "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/79/7b/2c79738432f5c924bef5071f933bcc9efd0473bac3b4aa584a6f7c1c8df8/mypy_extensions-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"

[packages.wheels.hashes]
sha256 = "1be4cccdb0f2482337c4743e60421de3a356cd97508abadd57d47403e94f5505"
```

uv skips the package:

```console
$ uv venv .venv
$ uv pip install --dry-run -r pylock.toml
warning: The `--pylock` option is experimental and may change without warning. Pass `--preview-features pylock` to disable this warning.
Checked in 0.01ms
Would make no changes
```

pip, same file, same interpreter, installs it:

```console
$ python -m pip install --dry-run -r pylock.toml
WARNING: Using pylock.toml as a requirements source is an experimental feature. It may be removed/changed in a future release without prior warning.
Collecting mypy-extensions==1.1.0 (from pylock.toml)
  Using cached mypy_extensions-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl (5.0 kB)
Would install mypy_extensions-1.1.0
```

#### Expected

`mypy-extensions` is installed, because `default-groups = ["mygroup"]` should seed `dependency_groups` and satisfy the marker.

#### Why there is no workaround

`--group mygroup` does resolve it:

```console
$ uv pip install --dry-run -r pylock.toml --group mygroup
 + mypy-extensions==1.1.0
```

But PEP 751 says of `default-groups`:

> The groups listed by this key SHOULD NOT be listed in `dependency-groups` as the groups are not meant to be directly exposed to users by name but instead via an installer's UI.

So a conforming locker is expected to keep these group names out of `dependency-groups`, and a consumer has no documented name to pass. The failure is also silent: exit code 0, no warning that packages were skipped.

#### Real-world impact

This is not hypothetical. `default-groups` exists for locks whose packages need a synthetic group to hang a marker on — PEP 751 describes it as representing "what should be installed by default (e.g. what `project.dependencies` implicitly represents)". Lockers use it for exactly that: `nab lock --project-default-group <name>` emits this shape, and such locks install under pip but are a silent no-op under uv.

#### Not a duplicate

[#14740](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/14740) was about uv failing to *parse* `dependency_groups` markers, fixed by [#14755](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/14755). Parsing and evaluation now work correctly — as the `--group mygroup` run above shows. This issue is only about the default seeding of `dependency_groups` from the lock's `default-groups` key.

I appreciate `--pylock` is experimental and the PEP requirement is SHOULD rather than MUST, so this may be a known gap. Flagging it mainly because uv and pip diverge on identical input and uv's side fails silently.

### Platform

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 GNU/Linux (Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2)

### Version

uv 0.12.17 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.14.5 (pip 26.1.1 for the comparison)
title: uv pip install -r pylock.toml ignores PEP 751 `default-groups`
